title: Rock a named midget fuse out of its open-clip block with a tong puller
instruction: The panel is de-energized. Pick up the yellow fuse puller, grip fuse F2 (CONTROL XFMR, the fuse with the orange label) in its jaws, lift the puller's handles to lever the near end of the fuse out of its clip first, then the far end, and drop the fuse in the blue parts tray. Do not disturb fuses F1 and F3.
context: Pulling cartridge fuses is regular work for electricians (SOC 47-2111) and industrial maintenance workers (49-9071, 49-9041): when troubleshooting a control panel they isolate it, remove a suspect fuse to test or replace it, and put the circuit back in service. On open-clip midget fuse blocks the fuse is taken out with an insulated tong puller rather than with fingers or pliers, and because the spring clips grip hard it is rocked out one end at a time: pulled straight, the puller slips off or the fuse jerks free and flies. Taking the wrong fuse cuts power to a circuit that is still needed (here the PLC supply or the cabinet light) and costs a second trip, so finding the named fuse and leaving its neighbours seated is part of doing the job right. A robot that can do this frees a qualified worker from a frequent, repetitive step of panel maintenance.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Panel: a light-grey 3 mm steel back pan (19 x 15 cm) lies flat on a 25 mm plywood board on the table, spanning 21.5 to 40.5 cm in front of the bases and 7.5 cm either side of the midline; its top face is 2.8 cm above the table. Fuse blocks: three Eaton Bussmann BM6031B one-pole midget fuse blocks (black, 76.2 x 21.0 x 30.7 mm; two tinned-copper spring clips 26.4 mm apart) are fixed to the pan side by side, 1.5 mm apart, their long axes pointing away from the robot and their centres 32.0 cm in front of the bases: F1 2.25 cm left of the midline, F2 on the midline, F3 2.25 cm right. Each holds a 10 x 38 mm midget fuse (Bussmann KTK class: 10.3 mm nickel-plated ferrules, fibre tube, 9 g) with its axis 5.3 cm above the table. Labels: a 34 x 20 mm circuit label lies on the pan in front of each block, centred 26.1 cm in front of the bases: 'F1 PLC 24V DC' on white, 'F2 CONTROL XFMR' on orange, 'F3 CABINET LIGHT' on green. Puller: an Ideal 34-015 one-piece yellow nylon tong fuse puller (127 mm; arms joined at a loop at the jaw end, curved jaws 13-27 mm from the loop, free handle ends; jaws sprung open) lies level on a grey two-pad rest 10.5 cm right of the midline, its loop end 34.6 cm and its handle ends 21.9 cm in front of the bases, the arms' undersides 6.4 cm above the table. Tray: a blue parts tray (10 x 10 cm inside, 2.5 cm walls) on the table, centred 21.5 cm in front of the bases and 19.0 cm right of the midline. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Milestones: 0.25 the puller is picked up (moved 2 cm or more from its rest); 0.5 then its jaws are closed on F2's body between the ferrules; 0.75 then F2 is out of both clips (each ferrule's centre 7 mm or more from its clip's centre, so the circuit is open) while held in the puller's jaws; 1.0 then F2 lies at rest inside the tray's walls. Cap: if F2 comes out of both clips at any moment without the puller's jaws on it (before 0.75 is reached), the score can be no more than 0.5 for the rest of the trial, even if the puller grips it afterwards and it ends in the tray. Hazard: the score is 0 for the whole trial, from the moment F1 or F3 moves in its clips (its centre 2 mm or more from where it sat, or tilted 4 degrees or more), even if milestones were already reached or are reached afterwards. Otherwise the score is the highest milestone reached. A reviewer checks positions with a rule, and from the video that F2 was in the jaws when it left its clips.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo finishes in 828 steps (41 s)
reset_notes: Press F2 back into its two clips (both ferrules seated, the label end toward the robot) and check that F1 and F3 are fully seated. Lay the puller back on its rest, jaw end away from the robot, and empty the tray. About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX at 480 Hz, rigid bodies; arms with the station's i2rt gains. Clip fingers are fixed faces 0.7 mm inside the ferrule (BMM603 STEP) with a compliant-contact spring (60 kN/m, friction 0.4): about 70 N to pull a fuse straight out, 33 N at one end (real force unpublished). Puller jaws, flex and opening inferred; jaw grip 1.0, smooth arms 0.25, notched handles 0.8; 34 g vs 20 g. Box/prism colliders; colour-coded labels. Details in README.
